criteria.criterion: A study directory (assumed studies/firstmate-work-handling/) holds typed records: pin (resolved SHA), claims, rationale cards, and a work-handling model, matching the study.*/1 schemas in docs/design/study-capability-m1.md.
criteria.evidence: The directory holds pin.json, claims.json, rationales.json, findings.json, model.json and validation.json, each tagged with a study.*/1 schema. But pin.json has "sha": "UNRESOLVED-PIN-SHA", and its how_resolved field says the producer could not read the resolved id. The criterion explicitly requires a resolved SHA, and design doc line 190 requires a 'full commit SHA' for study.pin/1.

criteria.criterion: Every claim about firstmate cites a file and line range (or run) in pinned-source/ with a quote; numbers are measured or labeled as estimates.
criteria.evidence: Every claim c01 to c40 (36 claims) has file sources with a path, start_line, end_line and quote. I grepped pinned-source/ for a sample of them, and each quote was found on the cited line: fm-spawn.sh:186, 195 and 3203; fm-watch.sh:365 and 367; AGENTS.md:33, 165, 196 and 369; SKILL.md:82. Numbers come from the source (exit 75, at most 3 attempts, relaunch bounded at 2), and the reversal costs in the rationale cards are labeled 'Estimate, not measured'. The citation SHA is the placeholder; that is covered under criterion 1.

criteria.criterion: The model covers how work enters, is assigned to the crew, progresses, is reviewed, and finishes or fails, with guards and each element evidenced.
criteria.evidence: model.json: entry (requested→queued, t1), assignment (t2 spawn, plus capacity deferral t3), progress (in-flight, t5/t6 captain decisions, t7 relaunch with the relaunches counter), review (pr-ready, t11 review steering, t9/t10 merge gates), finish (closing→done t13, scout t12) and failure (t8→failed, t14). Every state and transition lists claims and has a guard and the party that evaluates it. Unhandled failures and the concurrency section are also cited.

criteria.criterion: Any divergence between what firstmate's docs say and what it does is recorded as a contradicts-linked finding, and enforcement of each rule is marked as mechanism or prose-only.
criteria.evidence: Every claim text starts with an [enforcement: ...] tag; D78 explains that the schema has no field for it. Finding f3 and D78 state that no docs-versus-scripts divergence was found in the cited passages, so all contradicts arrays are empty. In my reading, the gaps in c19 and c23 (the captain's authority is not checked by the scripts) are correctly framed as prose-only enforcement, not as contradictions. One exception: c36 is tagged 'not examined', not mechanism or prose-only (reported as a minor finding).

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test --locked and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; both pass, and the study validation (every section 5.4 rule) reports pass with no offending ids.
criteria.evidence: Clippy and tests pass: every test-result line reported ok with 0 failed. validation.json lists 18 rules, all pass with empty offending lists. But D78 says that result came from a temporary test that was not kept, and grepping crates/ finds no test that loads studies/firstmate-work-handling, so the validation can't be rerun from this tree. Its wrong-sha pass is also meaningless here: rules.rs:268 only checks that each citation's SHA equals pin.sha, and both are the placeholder.
It exited 0, and the clippy and test commands chained after it with && then ran.

findings.summary: The pin is a placeholder, not a resolved commit SHA, so the study is not tied to any firstmate commit.
findings.evidence: "sha": "UNRESOLVED-PIN-SHA". The design (study-capability-m1.md:69 and :190) requires a full commit SHA, and all later steps read that SHA only. The CHANGELOG itself says it is 'to be replaced before publishing'. The tree is committed as a finished study anyway.
findings.location: studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json:6 and every "sha" in claims.json and rationales.json

findings.summary: The recorded validation result can't be reproduced, and the wrong-sha rule passes only because the placeholder matches itself.
findings.evidence: D78: 'a temporary test that read file text from pinned-source/; that test is not kept'. No file under crates/ references studies/firstmate-work-handling. rules.rs:268 compares src.sha to s.pin.sha, so a placeholder used in both places passes. The 'verified' default requires independent verification, which this tree does not allow.

Unrequested governance-adjacent edit: docs/non-rust-files.md gains a studies/** row.
findings.evidence: It is not in the expected deliverables. It is arguably needed to allow the new JSON files, and it is harmless.

summary: The study's content is solid. 36 claims about firstmate cite real lines in pinned-source/, and the quotes I sampled (fm-spawn.sh 186, 195 and 3203; fm-watch.sh 365 and 367; AGENTS.md 33, 165, 196 and 369; stuck-crewmate-recovery SKILL.md 82) match exactly. The model has 8 states and 14 transitions, and covers how work enters, is assigned, progresses, is reviewed, and finishes or fails, with guards and counters. cargo fmt, clippy and test all pass when I rerun them. The change still fails on its core deliverable. pin.json and all 50 file citations hold the placeholder "UNRESOLVED-PIN-SHA" instead of the resolved full commit SHA that criterion 1 and design section 190 require. Because of that, the wrong-sha rule passes only because the placeholder matches itself (rules.rs:268 compares each citation's SHA to the pin's), and nothing ties the study to a real firstmate commit. Also, validation.json was produced by a temporary test that was deleted (D78), and no test in the tree loads studies/firstmate-work-handling. So the claim that "all 18 rules pass" can't be reproduced from this tree. The pin needs to be resolved, for example from the job record that D75 writes, before this can pass.
